core_obligations: Reduce to X integral by the bivariant testing criterion (proof lines 12185-12193).
Match the two classes in the cases X = D and D different from X using the fundamental computation (proof lines 12195-12203).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to an integral base (proof lines 12185-12193).
difficulty_reason: For a triple (L, s, i : D -> X) as in Definition labelled definition-gysin-homomorphism over a base (S, delta), the lemma asserts that the Gysin homomorphism i^*, viewed in A^1(D -> X) by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-bivariant, equals the bivariant class c(D -> X, N) built from the virtual normal sheaf N = i^*L (statement lines 12173-12183). The proof uses the criterion of Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero to reduce to X integral, where it must show i^*[X] = c cap [X], and then splits into two cases (proof lines 12185-12193). If X = D both classes are represented by c_1(N) cap [X]_n with n = dim_delta(X), by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-fundamental and Definition labelled definition-gysin-homomorphism; if D is not X then D -> X is an effective Cartier divisor, in particular a regular closed immersion of codimension one, and Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-fundamental gives c(D -> X, N) cap [X]_n = [D]_{n-1}, which is also the definition of the Gysin homomorphism (proof lines 12195-12203). Reducing to an integral base and then matching the two cases with the fundamental computation is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
